# package amqp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport/amqp"
```

Package amqp is the AMQP transport of OPC UA PubSub (Part 14 §7.3.4 and Annex B.3): NetworkMessages (UADP or JSON) as AMQP 1.0 messages on a broker.

Importing the package registers the "amqp" and "amqps" schemes with [transport.Register](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/pubsub/transport#Register).

The URL is amqp://host\[:5672] or amqps://host\[:5671] (B.3.2); a path is ignored. Queue names (QueueName, MetaDataQueueName) are AMQP addresses: Send sends to the target address PublishOptions.Topic and Subscribe receives from the source address topic, without wildcards. How an address is resolved is up to the broker:

  - RabbitMQ 4 (native AMQP 1.0, address format v2): "/queues/\<queue>" sends to and receives from a declared queue; "/exchanges/\<exchange>/\<key>" sends to an exchange with a routing key, for example "/exchanges/amq.topic/opcua.data". Subscribers receive from a queue bound to the exchange.
  - ActiveMQ Artemis: a plain address, "opcua/data". It is created on first use; the routing type follows the broker's defaults or the "source-capabilities" / "target-capabilities" connection properties ("queue" for anycast, "topic" for multicast). The "queue://" and "topic://" prefixes work as well when the acceptor allows them.

Delivery guarantees (B.3.5): best effort and at most once (QoS 0) send pre-settled messages and receive on links the broker settles (a message can be lost); at least once (QoS 1) sends unsettled messages and Send returns when the broker accepted it (it is sent again after a reconnect, so it can arrive twice); exactly once is downgraded to at least once. DataSetMetaData is sent at least once. AMQP has no retained messages: PublishOptions.Retain is ignored, so a subscriber that starts late waits for the next metadata the publisher sends (MetaDataUpdateTime).

The message mapping follows B.3.7 and B.3.8: the body is one data section with the NetworkMessage, the properties carry a random UUID as message-id, the subject "ua-data" or "ua-metadata" and the content-type "application/opcua+uadp" or "application/json". The WriterGroupProperties and DataSetWriterProperties named in Table B.2 ("message-to", "message-reply-to", "message-correlation-id", "message-group-id", "message-reply-to-group-id", "message-content-encoding", "message-user-id", "message-absolute-expiry-time" (a Duration in milliseconds), "message-creation-time" (a Boolean)) set the message properties; the other properties become application-properties. Received messages may have any body that carries bytes (data sections, or an amqp-value or amqp-sequence holding binary).

The connection reconnects by itself with exponential backoff, attaches its links again and sends unsettled messages again; QoS 0 messages sent while it is reconnecting fail with ErrNotConnected.

Connection properties (KeyValuePairs of the PubSubConnection, B.3.4): "connection-hostname", "connection-max-frame-size" and "connection-idle-time-out" (milliseconds) set those fields of the open frame, "link-max-message-size" the limit of received messages; other names with the prefix "connection-", "session-" or "link-" are sent as properties of the open, begin and attach frames. Besides, "container-id", "username", "password", "sasl-mechanism" (ANONYMOUS, PLAIN, EXTERNAL or NONE), "source-capabilities" and "target-capabilities" (comma separated), "credit" (link credit of receivers) and "idle-timeout" (seconds) are honoured where the corresponding Config field is empty.

## Variables

ErrNotConnected is returned by a QoS 0 Send while the connection is re-established.

## Types

### type Conn

```go
type Conn struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Conn is an AMQP PubSub connection.

#### func Open

```go
func Open(ctx context.Context, cfg transport.Config) (*Conn, error)
```

Open connects to the broker of cfg.URL. Failed attempts are retried with backoff until ctx ends, except refusals a retry cannot fix (bad credentials, ...), so ctx should carry a deadline.

#### func (Conn) Close

```go
func (c *Conn) Close() error
```

Close closes the connection.

#### func (Conn) Connected

```go
func (c *Conn) Connected() bool
```

Connected reports whether the connection to the broker is up right now.

#### func (Conn) MaxMessageSize

```go
func (c *Conn) MaxMessageSize() int
```

MaxMessageSize is the largest payload Send accepts.

#### func (Conn) Send

```go
func (c *Conn) Send(ctx context.Context, payload []byte, opts transport.PublishOptions) error
```

Send sends payload to the address opts.Topic. QoS 0 sends it pre-settled, QoS 1 and 2 wait until the broker accepted it (and, while reconnecting, for the connection).

#### func (Conn) Subscribe

```go
func (c *Conn) Subscribe(ctx context.Context, topic string, qos byte, h transport.Handler) (func() error, error)
```

Subscribe receives the messages of the source address topic. QoS 0 receives on a link the broker settles, QoS 1 and 2 on one the client settles. The returned function detaches the link.
